title: What is known about 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LB_1LF0LC_1LB1RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LB_1LF0LC_1LB1RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the rightward pass for any block (kernel), no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps.

What it does. The head sweeps the whole tape. At the left end the tape is dense: blocks of 1s, almost all of length 4j+3, separated by single 0s. A fast rightward pass rewrites every block 14j+3 0 as the sparse word (1010)j 1000, the same length. A slow leftward zig-zag rebuilds dense blocks from the sparse words, but not the same ones: the list of block lengths is scrambled on every round trip, and a few cells are added at each end.

Where a halt would come from. Only A reading a 1 halts, which happens exactly after A>0 1 or 1 B>1. Neither has occurred; the content looks random, so a proof would need an invariant of the scrambling that nobody has found.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 35,832 cells have been visited and 24,371 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).

claims.title: Every way to a halt
claims.text: Two steps before any halt the machine is in A>0 1, 1 1 D>1 or 1 1 F>0; no other configuration halts within three steps.

claims.title: The rightward pass
claims.text: C crosses a dense block 14n+3 0 in 8n+6 steps and leaves the sparse word (1010)n 1000, for every n; two 1s cost four steps.

claims.title: The halting situations
claims.text: A>0 1 halts after two more steps and 1 B>1 after one: A writes a 1, B reads the next 1 and steps back onto a 1 in state A.

claims.title: Dense and sparse forms
claims.text: In the first 5·106 steps (464 round trips), at every left turn the tape is a list of 1-blocks separated by single 0s, and of the 72,345 blocks strictly inside the list 72,012 have length 4j+3 (235 have 4j+1, 98 are even: made near the left end and carried along). At every right turn the same list appears in sparse form, block 14j+30 of the previous left turn showing up as (0101)j0001, with the same rare exceptions.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The list of blocks behaves like the state of a cellular automaton; window closed-tape languages (K≤7) and run-length languages with lengths mod 4 both still allow a halt.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine shuttles its tape between two encodings, dense at the left end and sparse at the right end, and scrambles it a little on every trip. This page runs it in your browser and explains the two encodings.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 35,832 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Two encodings of one list
html: Run the simulator and look at the tape each time the head turns at an end. At the left end it is dense: runs of 1s separated by single 0s, nearly all of them of length 3, 7, 11, 15, … (4j+3). At the right end it is sparse: a string of the two 4-cell words x = 0101 and y = 0001.
The rightward pass is a plain translation. State C walks right and rewrites each dense block, two cells at a time:
Read from the other side, 14j+3 0 becomes xj y: the number j is kept, only the encoding changes. Lean proves this for every j (pass_block in lean/Rules.lean).

For example, at step 24,401 the dense blocks after the first have j = 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 3, 0, 4, 0, 4, 1, … and at the next right turn (step 24,720) the sparse words after the first read y, xy, y, y, xy, x3y, y, x4y, y, x4y, xy, …: the same numbers (py/forms.py show prints these lists).

sections.heading: The way back: a zig-zag that scrambles
html: The leftward trip is different. The head does not sweep straight back: it eats one sparse word, runs right to the end of the dense block it is building, comes back, and repeats. Each sparse word it eats lengthens or closes the block behind it. In the space-time diagram these trips are the saw-tooth edge on the left of each sweep.

The blocks it builds are not the blocks that came in. At step 24,401 the list was 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 3, 0, 4, …; one round trip later (step 25,402) it is 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 2, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, …. The rebuilding works like a carry rippling through the list, and over many round trips the list looks random: the long-time picture of the tape is noise, with no visible structure beyond the two encodings.

That is why this machine is hard. Halting needs A>0 1 or 1 B>1 (halt_A, halt_B), i.e. a local pattern that the encodings never contain; but whether the scrambling can ever produce one depends on the whole history, and no regular invariant (a closed tape language) small enough to search for has been found.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).
After 109 steps the tape spans 35,832 cells (19,704 left of the start, 6,677 right), with a density of 1s of 0.68.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: two-sided bouncer, dense/sparse translator with chaotic content
summary: Sweeps between a dense form (blocks 1<sup>4j+3</sup> 0) at the left end and a sparse form (words 0101, 0001) at the right end; the list of blocks changes chaotically from sweep to sweep. Open.
